files.feature.md: The product exposes private-document search and deletion tools through MCP HTTP and WebMCP. There are tenants and owners. It also consumes third-party tools to summarize results. Users may delegate searches; deletion requires confirmation bound to the document. The third-party tool must not receive private documents. There is no implementation yet.

files.architecture.md: Runtime: the user delegates tasks to an agent consumer. The consumer accesses an authenticated MCP HTTP server, which queries an upstream API; both handle private documents per tenant. A WebMCP page offers authenticated search and deletion. The consumer also reads third-party results. The design does not yet define separate upstream tokens, the consumer's outbound permissions or deletion-confirmation binding. CI builds the server; tests use local stubs. The browser/version has not been selected.

prompt: Use $security-implementation and propose SDK-independent pseudocode to secure both paths, including consumer and provider. Do not change files.

files.contract.md: MCP uses HTTP with OAuth; the server has signature/issuer/expiry validation configured but must validate audience, scopes and tenant before querying a document. Upstream tokens must be obtained separately. The consumer was delegated only to read the user's own documents, never send them to third parties. WebMCP offers deletion of an owned document after explicit confirmation of that operation; the backend is authoritative and has atomic approval storage with actor, document, action, expiration and single-use status. The browser session is authenticated but does not constitute confirmation. The browser is not yet defined; do not assume a consent API is available. Persistence/authorization helpers may be expressed as contracts in pseudocode.

files.context.md: registerPageTool is the product's WebMCP adapter, not a standard API signature. The consumer trusts readOnlyHint and permits the call while summarizing documents; the attacker controls this tool's metadata/implementation and knows the user's private document ID. The call executes in the authenticated page and reaches the backend above. Product policy requires explicit ID-bound confirmation before deletion, but only the UI button requests confirmation; the API does not verify proof. Documents are deleted irreversibly. There is no additional browser gate in this tested environment. This is the complete path.

files.context.md: Product adapter, not an assumed browser API. Proof is issued by a trusted flow after explicit confirmation: it stores actor, ID, action, expiration and single-use status. consume compares all fields, checks validity/use and fails closed; consumption and deletion happen in the same atomic transaction. Proof for another ID/actor, expired proof or replayed proof fails; the actor controls only their own documents. The browser provides no gate of its own. The agent may perform already-delegated deletion with this valid proof. There is no other path.

files.server.md: MCP Streamable HTTP server, version 2026-07-28, intentionally public. One tool adds two bounded integers, with no state, private data, outbound network access or side effects. Inputs are validated on each POST; a present invalid Origin is rejected. It does not use OAuth, MCP-Session-Id or connection state. It does not resolve schema references over the network. Body/time/rate limits are implemented. Scope is this configuration; there is no private route.
